## Country guides

### Potato Chips in Argentina: Brands, Flavors & Culture

URL: https://worldofchips.com/argentina/

- **Leading brands:** Lay's, Pehuamar, Krachitos, Quento and Pringles
- **Signature flavors:** Clásicas (Salted), Jamón Serrano, Queso Crema y Cebolla and Ketchup
- **Unique flavors:** Asado, Chimichurri, Provoleta and Salame
- **Market size:** $0.6B
- **Per capita / year:** 0.7 kg
- **Average bag price:** ARS 800/bag
- **Annual growth:** 3.5%
- **Typical occasions:** Pre-asado picada & copetín with vermouth or fernet, Afternoon mate & park gatherings, Football viewing (previa del partido) and Weekend family lunches
- **Notable fact:** PepsiCo built its Argentine chip business in the 1990s by acquiring local pioneer Bun (founded in 1958) in 1993 and Mar del Plata's Pehuamar (founded in 1964) in 1997, while domestic family rival Krachitos holds 15–20% of the market.
- **Where to buy:** Online via Amazon (e.g. Lay's & Latin American Potato Chips and Chimichurri & Asado Seasoned Kettle Chips)

**Q: What are the most popular potato chip brands in Argentina?**
A: The leading potato chip brands in Argentina are Lay's, Pehuamar, Krachitos, Quento and Pringles, with Lay's at the top. They compete for shelf space in supermarkets, convenience stores and online. Argentina's chip market is listed at $0.6B, with an average bag price of ARS 800/bag.

**Q: What potato chip flavors are popular in Argentina?**
A: The bestselling, most widely available flavors in Argentina are Clásicas (Salted), Jamón Serrano, Queso Crema y Cebolla and Ketchup. For something more distinctive, look for local specialities such as Asado, Chimichurri, Provoleta and Salame. Chips are typically eaten during pre-asado picada & copetín with vermouth or fernet, afternoon mate & park gatherings and football viewing (previa del partido).

**Q: What makes potato chips in Argentina unique?**
A: S. potato-chip boom (soon adding Kesbun cheese snacks). PepsiCo built its Argentine chip business in the 1990s by acquiring local pioneer Bun (founded in 1958) in 1993 and Mar del Plata's Pehuamar (founded in 1964) in 1997, while domestic family rival Krachitos holds 15–20% of the market.

**Q: Where can I buy chips from Argentina outside the country?**
A: The easiest option is online: World of Chips lists Amazon picks for chips from Argentina, including Lay's & Latin American Potato Chips, Chimichurri & Asado Seasoned Kettle Chips and Lay's 4-Flavor Variety Pack (40 bags). For more options, see our guides: Best international chip variety packs. As an Amazon Associate, World of Chips earns from qualifying purchases.

### Potato Chips in Egypt: Brands, Flavors & Culture

URL: https://worldofchips.com/egypt/

- **Leading brands:** Chipsy (Lay's), Tiger, Spuds, Doritos and Pringles
- **Signature flavors:** Kebab, Shatta & Lemon (Chili & Lemon), Tomato and Salt & Vinegar
- **Unique flavors:** Kebab, Shatta & Lemon, Spiced Tomato and Prime Ribs
- **Market size:** $0.7B
- **Per capita / year:** 0.3 kg
- **Average bag price:** EGP 15/bag
- **Annual growth:** 6.0%
- **Typical occasions:** Pairing with koshary, foul & ta'meya sandwiches, Ramadan post-iftar & suhoor gatherings, Football viewing at cafés & home and Mediterranean North Coast beach snacking
- **Notable fact:** Founded in 1982, PepsiCo Egypt's Chipsy holds around 60% of the country's snack market, sources 100% of its potatoes from Egyptian farms, and is so ubiquitous that Egyptians call any bag of potato chips 'chipsy'.
- **Where to buy:** Online via Amazon (e.g. Middle Eastern Spiced Potato Chips (Kebab & Chili Lemon) and Lay's Limón Tangy Citrus Chips (12.5 oz))

**Q: What are the most popular potato chip brands in Egypt?**
A: The leading potato chip brands in Egypt are Chipsy (Lay's), Tiger, Spuds, Doritos and Pringles, with Chipsy (Lay's) at the top. They compete for shelf space in supermarkets, convenience stores and online. Egypt's chip market is listed at $0.7B, with an average bag price of EGP 15/bag.

**Q: What potato chip flavors are popular in Egypt?**
A: The bestselling, most widely available flavors in Egypt are Kebab, Shatta & Lemon (Chili & Lemon), Tomato and Salt & Vinegar. For something more distinctive, look for local specialities such as Kebab, Shatta & Lemon, Spiced Tomato and Prime Ribs. Chips are typically eaten during pairing with koshary, foul & ta'meya sandwiches, ramadan post-iftar & suhoor gatherings and football viewing at cafés & home.

**Q: What makes potato chips in Egypt unique?**
A: In Egypt, "chipsy" (شيبسي) is not just a brand name — it is the everyday Arabic noun for any bag of potato chips. That status goes back to Chipsy for Food Industries, founded in 1982 and acquired by PepsiCo in 2001.

### Potato Chips in France: Brands, Flavors & Culture

URL: https://worldofchips.com/france/

- **Leading brands:** Lay's, Bret's, Vico, Tyrrell's, Doritos and Sibell
- **Signature flavors:** Nature (Salted), Poulet Rôti, Emmental and Vinaigre
- **Unique flavors:** Chèvre & Piment d'Espelette, Comté, Camembert and Tartiflette
- **Market size:** $1.8B
- **Per capita / year:** 1.0 kg
- **Average bag price:** €2.50/bag
- **Annual growth:** 3.2%
- **Typical occasions:** Apéritif hour (l'heure de l'apéro) before dinner, Pique-niques & outdoor summer dining, Tortilla chips with salsa & guacamole at parties and Beach & vacation snacking
- **Notable fact:** French potato-chip consumption rose 42% over ten years (Circana/LSA), propelled by Brittany's family-owned Bret's (founded in 1995 in Saint-Gérand), which holds 23% of the market behind Lay's (26.5%) and ahead of 1955 Picardy pioneer Vico.
- **Where to buy:** Online via Amazon (e.g. Bret's French Potato Chips (Brittany) and Vico French Chips & Apéritif Snacks)

**Q: What are the most popular potato chip brands in France?**
A: The leading potato chip brands in France are Lay's, Bret's, Vico, Tyrrell's, Doritos and Sibell, with Lay's at the top. They compete for shelf space in supermarkets, convenience stores and online. France's chip market is listed at $1.8B, with an average bag price of €2.50/bag.

**Q: What potato chip flavors are popular in France?**
A: The bestselling, most widely available flavors in France are Nature (Salted), Poulet Rôti, Emmental and Vinaigre. For something more distinctive, look for local specialities such as Chèvre & Piment d'Espelette, Comté, Camembert and Tartiflette. Chips are typically eaten during apéritif hour (l'heure de l'apéro) before dinner, pique-niques & outdoor summer dining and tortilla chips with salsa & guacamole at parties.

**Q: What makes potato chips in France unique?**
A: France's potato-chip market has been transformed over the past decade by a boom in flavoured, regional and apéritif chips. 5% in volume after the pandemic and 42% over ten years, while the average supermarket aisle expanded from 108 to 120 chip references in five years.

URL: https://worldofchips.com/germany/

- **Leading brands:** Lorenz, Funny-Frisch, Chio, Pringles and Lay's
- **Signature flavors:** Paprika, Salted, Sour Cream and Cheese & Onion
- **Unique flavors:** Currywurst, Döner Kebab, Bratwurst and Ungarisch
- **Market size:** $2.9B
- **Per capita / year:** 1.5 kg
- **Average bag price:** €2.20/bag
- **Annual growth:** 2.1%
- **Typical occasions:** Beer garden snacking, TV evening (Feierabend), Football match viewing and Carnival & festival treats
- **Notable fact:** In 2017 Germans bought, statistically, 2.6 bags of funny-frisch Chipsfrisch ungarisch every second. The paprika classic has been on sale since 1968.
- **Where to buy:** Online via Amazon (e.g. funny-frisch Chipsfrisch ungarisch (150 g) and Lorenz Crunchips Paprika (175 g))

**Q: What are the most popular potato chip brands in Germany?**
A: The leading potato chip brands in Germany are Lorenz, Funny-Frisch, Chio, Pringles and Lay's, with Lorenz at the top. They compete for shelf space in supermarkets, convenience stores and online. Germany's chip market is listed at $2.9B, with an average bag price of €2.20/bag.

**Q: What potato chip flavors are popular in Germany?**
A: The bestselling, most widely available flavors in Germany are Paprika, Salted, Sour Cream and Cheese & Onion. For something more distinctive, look for local specialities such as Currywurst, Döner Kebab, Bratwurst and Ungarisch. Chips are typically eaten during beer garden snacking, tV evening (Feierabend) and football match viewing.

**Q: What makes potato chips in Germany unique?**
A: Germany's chip story has a military footnote: according to Lorenz, the first potato chips produced in the country came off Heinz Flessner's automated line in 1951 and went to American soldiers stationed there.

URL: https://worldofchips.com/india/

- **Leading brands:** Lay's, Balaji, Haldiram's, Bingo! and Uncle Chipps
- **Signature flavors:** India's Magic Masala, Classic Salted, American Style Cream & Onion and Masala Masti
- **Unique flavors:** Spanish Tomato Tango, Chaat Chaska, Pudina (Mint) Twist and Achaari Masti (Mango Pickle)
- **Market size:** $4.5B
- **Per capita / year:** 0.3 kg
- **Average bag price:** ₹20/bag
- **Annual growth:** 8.2%
- **Typical occasions:** Cricket match viewing, Chai-time snacking, Birthday parties and festivals and School canteen and after-school snacks
- **Notable fact:** Balaji Wafers is named after the Balaji temple at Rajkot's Astron Cinema, where the Virani brothers ran the canteen and first sold their wafers to moviegoers.
- **Where to buy:** Online via Amazon (e.g. Lay's India's Magic Masala (52 g) and Balaji Masala Masti (150 g, 3-pack))

**Q: What are the most popular potato chip brands in India?**
A: The leading potato chip brands in India are Lay's, Balaji, Haldiram's, Bingo! and Uncle Chipps, with Lay's at the top. They compete for shelf space in supermarkets, convenience stores and online. India's chip market is listed at $4.5B, with an average bag price of ₹20/bag.

**Q: What potato chip flavors are popular in India?**
A: The bestselling, most widely available flavors in India are India's Magic Masala, Classic Salted, American Style Cream & Onion and Masala Masti. For something more distinctive, look for local specialities such as Spanish Tomato Tango, Chaat Chaska, Pudina (Mint) Twist and Achaari Masti (Mango Pickle). Chips are typically eaten during cricket match viewing, chai-time snacking and birthday parties and festivals.

**Q: What makes potato chips in India unique?**
A: Branded potato chips in India date back to 1992, when Amrit Agro launched Uncle Chipps, a pioneer of the category famous for its jingle "Bole mere lips, I love Uncle Chipps". PepsiCo brought Lay's to India in 1995, sold small packs from ₹5 to ₹25 and won shoppers over with local flavours, above all India's Magic Masala, the spicy, tangy "blue Lay's".

### Potato Chips in Japan: Brands, Flavors & Culture

URL: https://worldofchips.com/japan/

- **Leading brands:** Calbee, Koikeya, Lay's and Pringles
- **Signature flavors:** Usushio, Consommé and Nori-Shio
- **Unique flavors:** Wasabi, Matcha, Teriyaki Mayo, Sakura Shrimp and Mentaiko
- **Market size:** $3.2B
- **Per capita / year:** 1.6 kg
- **Average bag price:** ¥250/bag
- **Annual growth:** 3.5%
- **Typical occasions:** Konbini snacking, Izakaya accompaniment, Train journey snacks and Limited-edition collecting
- **Notable fact:** Calbee always has 50+ potato chip varieties on sale and releases around 100 flavors a year counting limited and regional editions.
- **Where to buy:** Online via Amazon (e.g. Calbee Japanese Chips and Calbee Consommé Punch)

**Q: What are the most popular potato chip brands in Japan?**
A: The leading potato chip brands in Japan are Calbee, Koikeya, Lay's and Pringles, with Calbee at the top. They compete for shelf space in supermarkets, convenience stores and online. Japan's chip market is listed at $3.2B, with an average bag price of ¥250/bag.

**Q: What potato chip flavors are popular in Japan?**
A: The bestselling, most widely available flavors in Japan are Usushio, Consommé and Nori-Shio. For something more distinctive, look for local specialities such as Wasabi, Matcha, Teriyaki Mayo, Sakura Shrimp and Mentaiko. Chips are typically eaten during konbini snacking, izakaya accompaniment and train journey snacks.

**Q: What makes potato chips in Japan unique?**
A: Japan's chip story starts with seaweed, not salt. In August 1962 Koikeya launched Koikeya Potato Chips Nori Shio, deliberately seasoned with a flavour Japanese snackers already knew, and in 1967 the company became the first in Japan to mass-produce potato chips. Calbee always has 50+ potato chip varieties on sale and releases around 100 flavors a year counting limited and regional editions.

A: The easiest option is online: World of Chips lists Amazon picks for chips from Japan, including Calbee Japanese Chips, Calbee Consommé Punch and Koikeya Karamucho Hot Chili. For more options, see our guides: Best Japanese chips to buy online and Best international chip variety packs. As an Amazon Associate, World of Chips earns from qualifying purchases.

A: The leading potato chip brands in Mexico are Sabritas (Lay's), Barcel, Takis and Totis, with Sabritas (Lay's) at the top. They compete for shelf space in supermarkets, convenience stores and online. Mexico's chip market is listed at $2.1B, with an average bag price of $1.20/bag.

**Q: What potato chip flavors are popular in Mexico?**
A: The bestselling, most widely available flavors in Mexico are Chile & Limón, Salsa Verde, Jalapeño and Adobadas. For something more distinctive, look for local specialities such as Esquites, Chamoy, Tamarindo and Flamin' Hot con Limón. Chips are typically eaten during street food accompaniment, antojitos & casual meals and fiestas & family gatherings.

**Q: What makes potato chips in Mexico unique?**
A: Mexico's chip story starts with Sabritas. Pedro Marcos Noriega started the business in Mexico City in 1943, making snacks at home and delivering them by bicycle; the name blends sabrosas (tasty) and fritas (fried). Grupo Bimbo was once offered Sabritas and turned it down, co-founder Roberto Servitje has said. Its own snack arm, Barcel, later invented Takis.

- **Per capita / year:** 2.8 kg
- **Average bag price:** €2.00/bag
- **Annual growth:** 1.8%
- **Typical occasions:** Borrel drinks with beer, wine & tortilla nacho dips, Oranje & Eredivisie football viewing, King's Day (Koningsdag) celebrations and Friday & weekend family snacking
- **Notable fact:** Dutch potato chips began on 3 May 1958 in Broek op Langedijk as Smith Potato Crisps (later Smiths, and since January 2001 Lay's), where factory workers traditionally received a free bag of chips every Friday afternoon.
- **Where to buy:** Online via Amazon (e.g. Lay's Patatje Joppie & Dutch Chips and Chio Chips Paprika (3-pack))

**Q: What are the most popular potato chip brands in the Netherlands?**
A: The leading potato chip brands in the Netherlands are Lay's, Croky, Chio, Doritos and Pringles, with Lay's at the top. They compete for shelf space in supermarkets, convenience stores and online. Netherlands's chip market is listed at $0.6B, with an average bag price of €2.00/bag.

**Q: What potato chip flavors are popular in the Netherlands?**
A: The bestselling, most widely available flavors in the Netherlands are Naturel, Paprika, Bolognese and Cheese Onion. For something more distinctive, look for local specialities such as Patatje Joppie, Bitterbal, Frikandel Speciaal and Saté. Chips are typically eaten during borrel drinks with beer, wine & tortilla nacho dips, oranje & Eredivisie football viewing and king's Day (Koningsdag) celebrations.

**Q: What makes potato chips in the Netherlands unique?**
A: Industrial potato-chip production in the Netherlands began on 3 May 1958 in Broek op Langedijk (North Holland), when local potato growers looking for a new outlet for Langedijker tubers partnered with British crisp manufacturer Frank Smith to establish Smith Potato Crisps. Because Dutch shoppers stumbled over the English word "crisps", the company soon renamed the product Smiths Chips.

- **Per capita / year:** 3.2 kg
- **Average bag price:** £1.50/bag
- **Annual growth:** 2.8%
- **Typical occasions:** Pub snacking with pints, Packed lunch staple, Afternoon tea-time nibbles and Picnics & gatherings
- **Notable fact:** Walkers is actually Lay's — but the brand kept its UK name after acquisition. It's the UK's #1 crisp brand by far.
- **Where to buy:** Online via Amazon (e.g. Walkers Variety Multipack and Walkers Cheese & Onion)

**Q: What are the most popular potato chip brands in the United Kingdom?**
A: The leading potato chip brands in the United Kingdom are Walkers (Lay's), Tyrrell's, Kettle Chips, McCoy's and Pipers, with Walkers (Lay's) at the top. They compete for shelf space in supermarkets, convenience stores and online. United Kingdom's chip market is listed at $3.8B, with an average bag price of £1.50/bag.

**Q: What potato chip flavors are popular in the United Kingdom?**
A: The bestselling, most widely available flavors in the United Kingdom are Cheese & Onion, Salt & Vinegar, Ready Salted and Prawn Cocktail. For something more distinctive, look for local specialities such as Marmite, Roast Chicken, Worcester Sauce and Lamb & Mint. Chips are typically eaten during pub snacking with pints, packed lunch staple and afternoon tea-time nibbles.

**Q: What makes potato chips in the United Kingdom unique?**
A: Before the 1950s, British crisps came plain: Smith's sold them with a small blue twist of salt in the bag for snackers to sprinkle themselves — an idea Walkers revived decades later as Salt & Shake. Walkers itself was founded in Leicester in 1948 by butcher Henry Walker, whose first crisps were salted and sold for threepence a bag.

### Potato Chips in the United States: Brands, Flavors & Culture

URL: https://worldofchips.com/united-states/

- **Leading brands:** Lay's, Ruffles, Pringles, Kettle Brand, Cape Cod and Utz

- **Market size:** $11B
- **Per capita / year:** 1.8 kg

- **Annual growth:** 5.7%

- **Notable fact:** Fredric Baur, the Procter & Gamble chemist who designed the Pringles can, was so proud of it that when he died in 2008 his family buried part of his ashes in one.
- **Where to buy:** Online via Amazon (e.g. Lay's 4-Flavor Variety (40 bags) and Utz Snack Variety Pack (42 ct))

**Q: What are the most popular potato chip brands in the United States?**
A: The leading potato chip brands in the United States are Lay's, Ruffles, Pringles, Kettle Brand, Cape Cod and Utz, with Lay's at the top. They compete for shelf space in supermarkets, convenience stores and online. United States's chip market is listed at $11B, with an average bag price of $4.50/bag.

**Q: What potato chip flavors are popular in the United States?**
A: The bestselling, most widely available flavors in the United States are Sour Cream & Onion, BBQ, Cheddar & Sour Cream and Salt & Vinegar. For something more distinctive, look for local specialities such as Flamin' Hot, Dill Pickle, Honey BBQ and Swicy. Chips are typically eaten during sporting events & tailgating, movie nights & casual snacking and lunch pairing with sandwiches.

**Q: What makes potato chips in the United States unique?**
A: America turned the potato chip into a mass-market snack. The popular origin story places it at Moon's Lake House near Saratoga Springs, New York, in 1853, where cook George Crum is said to have fried paper-thin "Saratoga Chips" for a fussy diner; historians point to earlier recipes, but agree Crum helped popularise them.

## Buyer's guides

### Best Asian Snack Boxes 2026: Bokksu vs TokyoTreat vs Daebak & More

URL: https://worldofchips.com/snack-boxes/

Bokksu vs TokyoTreat vs Sakuraco vs Daebak vs Japan Candy Box vs Universal Yums: verified 2026 prices, what’s inside, shipping to Europe, and the best box for chip lovers.

**Q: What is the best Japanese snack box in 2026?**
A: It depends on what you like. For traditional, artisan snacks and tea, Bokksu ($32.99–$39.99 a box) and its closest rival Sakuraco ($32.50–$37.50) lead. For full-size modern candy, KitKats and chips, TokyoTreat ($32.50–$37.50) is the pick. On a budget, Japan Candy Box starts at $25 a box on a 12-month plan. Shipping is extra for all of them.

**Q: TokyoTreat vs Bokksu: what is the difference?**
A: TokyoTreat sends 12–15 full-size, mostly big-brand modern Japanese snacks (KitKat, Pocky, chips, noodles, gacha) for $32.50–$37.50 a box plus $16.99 shipping. Bokksu sends 20–22 snacks plus a tea, mostly from small traditional makers, for $32.99–$39.99 a box plus $13.99 (US) or $15.99 (UK/EU/Canada/Australia) shipping. Pick TokyoTreat for pop snacks and chips, Bokksu for an artisan, gift-style box.

**Q: Which snack box has the most chips and savory snacks?**
A: Daebak’s Korean SnackFever box (chips and crackers in every box) and TokyoTreat (a dedicated chips and salty treats category) are the most savory-friendly. Bokksu and Japan Candy Box include some chips and rice crackers; Sakuraco is mostly traditional sweets. No company promises a set number of chips per box.

**Q: Is there a Korean snack box?**
A: Yes. Daebak’s SnackFever ships Korean convenience-store snacks from Seoul: 8+ snacks for $40 (Original) or 12+ for $55 (Deluxe). It is seasonal (four boxes a year), with 10% off on a seasonal subscription or 15% off on an annual plan. Universal Yums also lets you pick South Korea as your first box (US and Canada only).

**Q: Which snack boxes ship to Europe, and will I pay customs?**
A: Bokksu ($15.99 a box to the UK and EU), TokyoTreat and Sakuraco ($16.99), Daebak (from $6.99) and Japan Candy Box (fee shown at checkout) all ship to Europe. Universal Yums does not. Daebak includes VAT and duties in its shipping price. TokyoTreat and Sakuraco collect EU VAT at checkout but warn that customs duty may be charged on delivery since the EU dropped its low-value duty exemption on 1 July 2026. Bokksu and Japan Candy Box say EU buyers may have to pay duties or VAT on import.

**Q: What happened to Japan Crate?**
A: Japan Crate has shut down its snack box. Its homepage now shows a farewell message and points former subscribers to Bokksu and Sugoi Mart. If you want a similar monthly box, look at TokyoTreat (modern snacks) or Bokksu (traditional snacks).

**Q: Is Sakuraco the same company as TokyoTreat?**
A: Sakuraco is TokyoTreat’s sister box. TokyoTreat lists it among its brands, the two share a help center and shipping table, and they currently have the same plan prices. The boxes are very different, though: Sakuraco focuses on traditional sweets, tea and a home good; TokyoTreat on modern snacks.

**Q: What is the cheapest snack box subscription?**
A: Universal Yums’ smallest Yum Box costs $18–$20 a month with free shipping in the contiguous US (US and Canada only). For a Japan-only box, Japan Candy Box starts at $25 a box on a 12-month plan, plus shipping.

### Best Japanese Chips to Buy Online in 2026: Calbee, Koikeya & More

URL: https://worldofchips.com/best-japanese-chips/

The Japanese potato chips worth ordering online: Calbee Usushio, Norishio and Consommé Punch, Koikeya Karamucho and more, with launch dates, what each tastes like and where to buy.

**Q: What is the most popular Japanese chip brand?**
A: Calbee is Japan’s best-known potato chip maker; its first potato chip, Usushio (lightly salted), launched in 1975. Koikeya is the other big name and is even older in chips: it launched its Norishio seaweed-salt chip in 1962.

**Q: What does Consommé Punch taste like?**
A: It is seasoned like a consommé broth: savoury, meaty and oniony rather than salty-sour. Calbee launched it in 1978 and it sold as plain “Consommé” between 1980 and 1992.

**Q: Are Karamucho chips very spicy?**
A: Karamucho is Koikeya’s hot-chilli chip, made since 1984. Koikeya describes it as chilli heat mixed with a meat-and-vegetable savoury flavour, so it is noticeably hot but rounder than a pure chilli chip.

**Q: Why are Japanese chips so expensive on Amazon?**
A: Most listings are imported multipacks sold by third-party sellers, so you pay for shipping and handling as well as the chips. Compare price per ounce and buy larger packs to get a better unit price.

### Where to Buy Takis & Honey Butter Chip in Europe (2026)

URL: https://worldofchips.com/where-to-buy-asian-chips-europe/

Which UK supermarkets stock Takis, which EU online shops sell Haitai Honey Butter Chip and at what price, and how to get Japanese and Korean chips delivered in Europe. Checked October 2026.

**Q: Can you buy Takis in the UK?**
A: Yes. According to Takis Near Me (updated September 2026), Morrisons, Co-op, Iceland, Farmfoods and Aldi (as a Specialbuy) stock Takis. Tesco, Sainsbury’s, Asda and Lidl did not carry them as a regular range in 2026.

**Q: Where can I buy Honey Butter Chip in Europe?**
A: EU online Asian grocers such as Nanuko (€2.79), Aasia Market (€3.20), MAOMAO and World of Sweets (€3.49 each) and Phomifood (€3.93) listed the 60 g bag when we checked on 22 October 2026. Shipping is extra.

**Q: Do I pay customs on snacks ordered from the US or Asia?**
A: Possibly. The EU dropped its duty exemption for parcels under €150 on 1 July 2026, so duty and VAT may be due on delivery. Ordering from a shop that ships from within the EU avoids this.

### Best International Chip Variety Packs & Where to Buy World Chips Online (2026)

URL: https://worldofchips.com/best-international-chip-variety-packs/

Where to buy international-flavor potato chips online in 2026: Amazon exotic chip variety packs vs. subscription snack boxes, verified prices, and how to avoid stale or overpriced bundles.

**Q: What is the best place to buy international-flavor potato chips online?**
A: If you only want potato chips and want to pick exact flavours (such as Chinese Lay’s Cucumber, Japanese Calbee Consommé Punch, Korean Haitai Honey Butter Chip or British Walkers Cheese & Onion), Amazon variety packs and à-la-carte Asian grocers (like Japan Candy Store worldwide, or Nanuko and World of Sweets inside the EU) are the best choice. If you want a curated surprise box of 10–20 snacks from a country, subscription boxes like TokyoTreat, Daebak SnackFever, Bokksu and Universal Yums lead.

**Q: Why do Chinese Lay’s chips in variety packs look expired?**
A: Food packaging in mainland China prints the manufacturing date (production date) on the bag rather than the expiration date. Most Chinese Lay’s potato chips have a shelf life of 6 to 9 months from that printed date. Japanese, Korean, British and EU bags print the best-before date instead.

**Q: Which snack box has the most international potato chips?**
A: Among subscription boxes we checked in October 2026, Daebak’s Korean SnackFever box ($40 Original / $55 Deluxe per seasonal box, with chips and crackers in every box) and Japan’s TokyoTreat ($32.50–$37.50/box, with a dedicated chips and salty treats category among its 12–15 full-size items) are the strongest picks for chip lovers. Universal Yums ($18–$47/box, US and Canada only) rotates to a new country each month and includes savoury chips and crackers alongside sweets.

**Q: How much do imported chips cost on Amazon?**
A: Expect to pay roughly $4 to $5 per small 55–60 g imported bag when buying multipacks on Amazon.com: for example, when we checked on 22 October 2026, a 3-pack of 2.11 oz Haitai Honey Butter Chips was $14.50 ($4.83/bag) and a 12-pack of 2.01 oz Koikeya Karamucho Hot Chili was $49.98 ($4.17/bag), because air/sea freight and importer handling are built into the price.
